bills.title: VEH CD-PLATES-REGISTRATION
bills.detail: Amends the Illinois Vehicle Code. Sets forth titling requirements for (i) a motor driven cycle that is powered by an electric motor with a nominal power rating of greater than 750 watts but less than or equal to 8,000 watts and (ii) a gas-powered bicycle capable of operating at speeds greater than 28 miles per hour. Excludes electric micromobility devices from titling, registration, license or permit, and liability insurance policy requirements. Establishes signage requirements notifying users of areas where the operation of motor driven cycles is strictly prohibited. Sets forth the operation of toy vehicles, motor driven cycles, and electric micromobility devices in the State. Prohibits low-speed gas bicycles and low-speed electric bicycles from being operated by a person under the age of 18 with a passenger unless the passenger is a sibling, stepsibling, child, or stepchild of the operator. Establishes where a low-speed gas bicycle may be operated. Allows the Department of Natural Resources and park districts, forest preserve districts, conservation districts, and transit districts to regulate the use of low-speed electric bicycles on their properties. Defines terms. Makes other changes. Makes conforming changes in the Micromobility Fire Safety Act and the Consumer Fraud and Deceptive Business Practices Act. Effective January 1, 2027.

label: Week 35, 2026
recap:
This week's state level AI activity showed 17 bill movements and 11 case updates, with no federal documents recorded. Activity was concentrated in California, which accounted for 12 of the tracked bills, while Michigan saw 3, and Illinois and New Jersey each had 1. The thematic spread was led by health care and infrastructure and energy, each with 4 bills, followed by transparency and disclosure with 3, and children and minors, consumer protection and discrimination, and employment and hiring each with 2. Criminal law and government use each appeared once, and 2 bills were unthemed.

Overall, the week's movement reflected changes in bill status rather than any final passage, spread across a modest number of jurisdictions. With four states represented and a relatively small total of updates, this was a quiet week in the broader record, showing incremental procedural activity rather than major legislative or judicial developments in AI policy.
